pr.title: State that every reviewed pull request gets a summary
pr.head: 68c778d8c81c73f7e80045e3f30c7142b19e8899

summary: Projector's review loop reviews each pull request head with the review-pr skill. After it publishes a review, it writes a summary: a guided page on the repository's Projector site that walks a human reviewer through the diff. project summary publish posts that page, then links it from a comment on the pull request and from a link block, two lines it appends to the end of the pull request's description.

review-pr already said to summarize after every review. Agents still doubted that rule once the description edit appeared. One subagent brief said never to edit the pull request body, so subagents stalled at the publish. One subagent deleted the link block by hand. A loop lead held summaries on other authors' pull requests, which are the ones whose reviewers need a summary most.

This change states the rule in each place an agent would doubt it. It also adds --no-describe to project summary publish, so that a repository whose instructions forbid agents to edit descriptions still gets a summary, linked from the pull request comment alone.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Summary: the JSON a review writes, which the Projector site renders as a guided page.
  • Summaries ref: refs/projector/summaries, a hidden Git ref that stores each summary at summaries/<number>/<head>/summary.json.
  • Link block: the marker comment and link line that publish appends to the description.
  • Brief: the instructions a loop lead writes for each reviewing subagent.

cards.title: Review state at this head

groups.title: Every reviewed pull request gets a summary
groups.kicker: Where a review subagent and the loop lead learn that the summary is not optional
intro: A review summarizes when two conditions hold: review.summarize is not false, and the repository hosts a Projector site. The new text in review-pr says that, while both hold, nothing else skips the summary. That includes the pull request's author, a brief, and the agent's own judgment. The one off switch is review.summarize = false in .projector.toml.

It also says that the description edit is deliberate. publish removes any earlier link block and appends a new one at the very end, below a trailer such as Ticket:. A brief that bans body edits does not cover the link block. A repository's own instructions do: where they forbid agents to edit descriptions, the review publishes with --no-describe, so the summary still goes out and the comment alone links it. start-review-loop repeats both rules for the loop lead.

files.note: The "Summarize the pull request" section gains the no-skip rule, a paragraph on the description edit, and the --no-describe rule for a repository that forbids description edits.

checks.text: The paragraph matches describe_summary in src/projector/summary.py. That function removes every earlier link block with SUMMARY_BLOCK.sub, trims trailing whitespace, and appends the new block after a blank line. So the block ends the description, and a block moved or deleted by hand returns to the end on the next publish.

describe_summary is the only code that edits the description, and run_summary skips it under --no-describe. So this flag is enough to honor a repository rule against description edits without losing the summary.

The "Update rather than start over" bullet now starts from the newest summary of the pull request, even one at this same head or one another account published. summarize-pr gives the commands that find it.

files.note: The subagent section tells the loop lead never to hold summaries on its own judgment.

groups.title: A publish that leaves the description alone
groups.kicker: The --no-describe flag on project summary publish
intro: On a hosted site, project summary publish links the summary twice: from a comment on the pull request, written by comment_summary, and from a link block at the end of the description, written by describe_summary. The new --no-describe flag keeps the push and the comment and skips only the description edit. It prints a line saying it left the description alone.

files.note: Adds the flag to the summary publish parser, and skips describe_summary in run_summary when it is set.

checks.text: The flag sits inside the hosted branch, so --local, which has no site, still posts neither link. The new test runs this path with a hosted site and sees the push and the comment, with no description edit.

files.note: One test for --no-describe through the CLI, with publish, comment_summary, and describe_summary mocked.
Documents --no-describe beside the description link it skips.

groups.title: Updating starts from the newest published summary
groups.kicker: How an update finds the summary another session already wrote
intro: Another session, or another account, can already have summarized the pull request, at an earlier head or at this one. The new opening of "Update the page when the pull request moves" says to start from that summary, and gives three commands. The first fetches the summaries ref. The second finds the folder that the newest commit on the ref wrote for the pull request. The third copies that folder's summary.json.
Each publish commits one folder, so the newest commit that touches summaries/NUMBER/ names one head.

files.note: A new opening paragraph and recipe for finding the newest summary before step 1.

checks.text: The fetch reads the ref on origin. In a repository that does not host its site, publish pushes nothing and keeps summaries in the checkout's own refs/projector/summaries, so this fetch fails there. The review lists that as a suggestion.

summary_tree and publish in src/projector/summary.py write one folder per commit on a linear history. A publish that loses the race for the ref rebuilds its commit on the new tip, still with one folder, and the legacy carry-over replays the old commits one by one. So git log -1 limited to the pull request's folder names a single head.
